Match: (a) Visible spectrum — ? (b) Far infrared — ? [Lyman / Balmer / Paschen / Pfund]

questions.answer:
(a) True.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The energy of the electron in the nth orbit of hydrogen is ______ eV. (b) The ionization energy of hydrogen is ______ eV.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Write two postulates of Rutherford's atomic model.
questions.answer:
(1) All the positive charge and nearly all the mass of an atom are concentrated in a tiny central nucleus.
(2) Electrons revolve round the nucleus in orbits, the electrostatic attraction providing the centripetal force; most of the atom is empty space.

questions.q: Calculate the ratio of the energies of hydrogen in its first excited state and its second excited state.
questions.answer:
Eₙ = −13.6/n². First excited state n = 2: −3.4 eV. Second excited state n = 3: −1.51 eV.
E₂ : E₃ = (1/4) : (1/9) = 9 : 4.

questions.q: State Bohr's postulates.
questions.answer:
(1) Electrons revolve in certain stationary orbits without radiating energy.
(2) In these orbits the angular momentum is an integral multiple of h/2π: mvr = nh/2π.
(3) Energy is emitted or absorbed only when an electron jumps between orbits: hν = E_i − E_f.

questions.q: What were the drawbacks of Rutherford's model?
questions.answer: A revolving electron is accelerated, so by classical theory it should radiate energy continuously and spiral into the nucleus. Atoms would be unstable and would give a continuous spectrum — contrary to observed stable atoms and line spectra.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: A hydrogen atom makes a transition from n = 3 to n = 1. Find the wavelength emitted and name the series. (R = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹)
questions.answer:
1/λ = R(1/1² − 1/3²) = R × 8/9 = 1.097 × 10⁷ × 0.889 = 9.75 × 10⁶ m⁻¹.
λ ≈ 1.026 × 10⁻⁷ m = 102.6 nm.
The final level is n = 1, so it belongs to the Lyman series (ultraviolet).

questions.q: Describe Rutherford's α-scattering experiment and its conclusions.
questions.answer:
A narrow beam of α-particles from a radioactive source was directed at a thin gold foil; a zinc-sulphide screen detected the scattered particles at various angles.
Observations: most passed undeviated; a few were deflected through large angles; about 1 in 8000 bounced back.
Conclusions: the atom is mostly empty; its positive charge and mass are in a tiny nucleus (about 10⁻¹⁵ m); electrons revolve round it.

questions.q: Name the series of the hydrogen spectrum with their regions and the formula for each.
questions.answer:
1/λ = R(1/n₁² − 1/n₂²):
Lyman — n₁ = 1, ultraviolet.
Balmer — n₁ = 2, visible.
Paschen — n₁ = 3, infrared.
Brackett — n₁ = 4, infrared.
Pfund — n₁ = 5, far infrared.
In each series n₂ = n₁ + 1, n₁ + 2, …

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Using Bohr's postulates, show that the energy of the electron in the nth orbit of hydrogen is Eₙ = −13.6/n² eV.
questions.answer:
Centripetal force from electrostatic attraction: mv²/r = ke²/r² … (1)
Quantum condition: mvr = nh/2π … (2)
From (1) and (2): rₙ = n²h²/(4π²mke²) = n² × 0.53 Å, and v = 2πke²/nh.
KE = ½mv² = ke²/2r; PE = −ke²/r.
Total E = −ke²/2r = −2π²mk²e⁴/(n²h²).
Substituting the constants: Eₙ = −13.6/n² eV (−13.6 eV for n = 1, −3.4 eV for n = 2).
